The update and destroy methods in Admin::EmbeddableHostsController do not validate the existence of the EmbeddableHost record retrieved by ID. If EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first returns nil (i.e., the host does not exist), attempting to call methods on the nil object (e.g., save_host or destroy) will result in a NoMethodError.
record_for_host compares lower(host) = ? but does not normalize the parameter’s case, so mixed‑case referer hosts may fail to match even though comparison intends to be case‑insensitive.

Because this migration inserts embeddable_hosts rows with raw SQL, any existing embeddable_hosts values that include http:// or /https:// or path segments won’t go through the EmbeddableHost model’s normalization, so the new host lookup (which compares only the bare host) may fail for migrated data. Consider ensuring that migrated hosts are normalized to the same format as newly created EmbeddableHost records so existing embedding configurations keep working.

The migration accesses execute(...)[0]['id'] without checking if the query returned any rows, which causes a crash when no embed_category setting exists. This can lead to a broken feature when attempting to edit category/host relationships.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration create_embeddable_hosts.rb:15 has the same unguarded `[0]['value']` access on the `uncategorized_category_id` lookup, raising NoMethodError if the row is missing instead of degrading gracefully

adjudication.rationale: In db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb, when category_id == 0 it does: execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i. Unlike the later embeddable_hosts lookup, there is no cmd_tuples/row-present guard. If that SELECT returns zero rows, [0] will be nil and nil['value'] will raise NoMethodError, causing the migration to fail instead of handling the missing setting.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration uses `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`, which silently drops and recreates an existing table, causing unrecoverable data loss on re-run or when a plugin created the table

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateEmbeddableHosts` explicitly calls `create_table :embeddable_hosts, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop an existing `embeddable_hosts` table and recreate it, which would erase any existing data if the table already exists (e.g., from a prior migration, schema load mismatch, or a plugin). This data-loss behavior is directly present in the diff and is a reasonable correctness concern to flag.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Migration line 25 interpolates the host string raw into `INSERT ... VALUES ('#{h}', ...)`, so a host containing a single quote breaks the statement or injects SQL; should use quote/bind params

adjudication.rationale:
Real issue: in `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, the migration loops over `records.each do |h|` where `h` comes from the existing `site_settings` value `embeddable_hosts` (user-provided/admin-configurable text), and then runs:

```rb
execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
```

This directly interpolates `h` into a SQL string inside single quotes without quoting/escaping. A host containing a single quote (or other special characters) will break the SQL and could potentially alter the statement. Using `connection.quote(h)` or bind parameters would avoid both correctness breakage and injection risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host format validation allows an optional `:port` and before_validation preserves it, but `record_for_host` compares against `uri.host` which excludes the port, so entries like `example.com:3000` can never match

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbeddableHost`, the `host` field validation regex explicitly allows an optional `:port` (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and the `before_validation` callback strips scheme and path but does not remove the port, so a record like `example.com:3000` can be saved. However, `record_for_host` parses the incoming URL with `URI(host)` and then uses `uri.host`, which excludes the port, and compares that to `lower(host)` in the DB (`where("lower(host) = ?", host)`), so `example.com:3000` will never match an incoming referer like `http://example.com:3000/...` (it will compare `example.com` vs `example.com:3000`). This makes port-qualified allowed hosts effectively unusable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23 accesses `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without `params.require`, raising NoMethodError if the `embeddable_host` key is missing from the request body

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host the code directly dereferences nested params: `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `params[:embeddable_host][:category_id]`. If the request omits the `embeddable_host` key (e.g., malformed client request), `params[:embeddable_host]` will be nil and `nil[:host]` will raise a NoMethodError, causing a 500. The diff does not include any `params.require(:embeddable_host)` / guard to prevent this.

adjudication_records.issue_text: store.js.es6:196-201 `_ids` branch deletes `obj[k]` unconditionally and keeps `undefined` entries for unresolved ids, so non-sideloaded collections render blank rows instead of failing visibly; should mirror the singular branch and filter unresolved ids

adjudication.rationale: In `store.js.es6` `_hydrateEmbedded`, the new plural `_ids` handling (`if (m[2])`) does `const hydrated = obj[k].map(id => _lookupSubType(...))` and then unconditionally assigns it to `obj[self.pluralize(subType)]` and unconditionally `delete obj[k]`. Since `_lookupSubType` can return `undefined`/`null` when a referenced id is not sideloaded in `root`, the resulting array will contain unresolved entries rather than filtering them out, and the original ids array is lost due to unconditional deletion. This differs from the singular branch, which only deletes `obj[k]` when hydration succeeded (`if (hydrated) ... delete obj[k]`). The core issue (keeping unresolved entries and deleting ids regardless) is directly present in the diff; the rendering symptom is plausible but the data-shape defect is verifiable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The `category_id` column is `null: false` but EmbeddableHost has no presence validation on `category_id`, so creation paths outside the controller raise NotNullViolation instead of a validation error

adjudication.rationale: Yes. The migration creates `embeddable_hosts.category_id` with `null: false` (db-level constraint), but the `EmbeddableHost` model only validates the `host` format and does not validate presence of `category_id`/`category`. As shown in `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb`, `EmbeddableHost.new(host: 'http://example.com')` is expected to `be_valid` even though it has no `category_id`; if such an instance were saved via any path that doesn't set a default (unlike `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host`, which forces uncategorized when blank), it would raise a DB NotNullViolation instead of producing a model validation error.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb and embedding_controller_spec.rb only assert class hierarchy, leaving create/update/destroy, the nil-record 500s, the missing-param crash, and the uncategorized-category fallback untested

adjudication.rationale: The two new controller specs (`spec/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/controllers/admin/embedding_controller_spec.rb`) only assert that the controllers subclass `Admin::AdminController` and do not exercise any controller actions. In the diff, `Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#update`/`#destroy` fetch a host with `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` and then immediately call `save_host(host)` / `host.destroy` without nil checks; if the record isn’t found this will raise `NoMethodError` and 500. Also `save_host` dereferences `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` and `[:category_id]` without guarding against missing `params[:embeddable_host]`, which would also raise. The uncategorized fallback logic (`host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?`) likewise isn’t covered by any spec. So the finding that these important behaviors/edge cases are untested is verifiably true from the diff and points at real crash-prone paths.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No unique index or model uniqueness validation on `host`, allowing duplicate hosts and forcing an unindexed `lower(host)` scan on every embed request

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `EmbeddableHost` with only a `validates_format_of :host` and a migration that creates `embeddable_hosts` without any index/unique constraint on `host`. Lookups are performed via `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` using `where("lower(host) = ?", host).first`, and `host_allowed?` is called in request paths like `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` and `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?`. With no supporting (functional) index, this case-insensitive `lower(host)` predicate will not be index-backed and will devolve to a scan as the table grows. Also, without model/db uniqueness enforcement, duplicate `host` rows are possible, and `.first` would pick an arbitrary record (potentially leading to inconsistent category selection).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host format regex `[a-z]{2,5}` for the TLD rejects valid hosts like foo.website, foo.technology and .travel, and also rejects `localhost:3000` which the old setting permitted

adjudication.rationale: The new `EmbeddableHost` model adds `validates_format_of :host` with a TLD restriction `\.[a-z]{2,5}` and requires at least one dot in the hostname. This will reject valid longer modern TLDs (e.g. `.travel` (6), `.website` (7), `.technology` (10)) and also reject `localhost` / `localhost:3000` entirely because it has no dot. Previously, embeddable host allowance was based on `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` which performed URI parsing and string comparison without this kind of strict hostname/TLD validation, so `localhost` could be allowed; the diff therefore introduces a real compatibility/correctness regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: adapters/rest.js.es6:22 uses `type.replace('_', '-')` with a string argument, replacing only the first underscore; should use a global regex `/_/g`

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `basePath(store, type)` to check `ADMIN_MODELS.indexOf(type.replace('_', '-'))`. While `String#replace('_','-')` only replaces the first underscore, all admin model names involved in this diff contain at most one underscore when using underscore form (e.g. `embeddable_host`, `site_customization`). Therefore, with the current `ADMIN_MODELS = ['plugin', 'site-customization', 'embeddable-host']`, this does not introduce a verifiable bug in the code as changed; it’s more of a future-proofing/style suggestion for hypothetical multi-underscore model names not present here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:44-50 `destroyRecord()` lacks `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, so a failed delete leaves the row rendered with no admin feedback

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6`, the `delete()` action calls `this.get('host').destroyRecord().then(() => { this.sendAction('deleteHost', this.get('host')); });` but does not attach a `.catch(popupAjaxError)` (unlike `save()`, which does). If the DELETE request fails, the promise rejection is unhandled and the UI provides no admin-visible error; additionally `deleteHost` is only sent on success so the row remains rendered with no feedback.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6:36 sets `category` from the local `categoryId` after save, so when the chooser is empty the badge shows undefined instead of the server-assigned uncategorized_category_id

adjudication.rationale: Yes. In admin/components/embeddable-host.js.es6 `save()` sets `props.category_id = this.get('categoryId')` and then, on success, unconditionally runs `host.set('category', Discourse.Category.findById(this.get('categoryId')));`. If the chooser is left empty, `categoryId` remains null, so the request sends a blank `category_id` and the server assigns `uncategorized_category_id` (see Admin::EmbeddableHostsController#save_host). However, the client then sets `host.category` using `findById(null)`, which results in `undefined` and the template `{{category-badge host.category}}` will render blank/undefined despite the server having assigned a real category_id.

adjudication_records.issue_text: admin/embedding_controller.rb:10-12 `update` ignores the request body and re-renders `show`, so PUT /admin/customize/embedding falsely reports success, and `saveChanges` in admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7 is dead code

adjudication.rationale: In Admin::EmbeddingController#update, the method simply re-renders the serialized @embedding (same as #show) and does not read params or persist any changes. The routes add a PUT /admin/customize/embedding endpoint, but this implementation is a no-op that will return 200/success JSON regardless of request body. On the client side, admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6 defines an action saveChanges() that calls this.get('embedding').update({}), but the provided embedding.hbs template contains no control wired to invoke saveChanges, so within this diff that action is unused/dead and the PUT would not have any effect if called.
